chapters.title: Chapter 2: The Taxonomy of Alternative Data

lessons.title: Supply Chain and Corporate Data: GST Filings, Import-Export Records, and Job Postings

body.text: A company files things with the government long before it files results with the exchange. This category is about reading those filings first.

children.text: This final lesson in the taxonomy chapter covers the regulatory exhaust of running a business in India: tax filings, customs records, hiring activity, and corporate registry entries, none of which were built for equity research, all of which leak real information about a company's activity ahead of its own quarterly disclosure.
Four Sources That Reveal What a Company Hasn't Said Yet

children.text: E-Way Bills as an Early Read on Industrial Activity

markDefs.definition: An electronic document required under India's GST framework for the movement of goods above a threshold value, generally ₹50,000, especially for interstate transport. It records the consignor, consignee, goods, and value of the shipment.

children.text: is generated every time a taxable shipment above the threshold moves, which means the aggregate e-way bill count is effectively a running tally of goods actually moving through the economy. State-wise and category-wise breakdowns of this data are published with far shorter lag than India's official Index of Industrial Production, which is why some economists and desks watch e-way bill trends as an early proxy for the direction of the next IIP print, particularly for manufacturing and logistics-heavy sectors.

stats.label: Trigger threshold
stats.context: The general threshold above which an e-way bill is required for a shipment

stats.label: What it proxies
stats.context: A running count of taxable goods movement, not a sales or revenue figure

stats.label: Relative to IIP
stats.context: Useful as an early directional read, not a precise substitute for the official industrial production index

children.text: Trade and Customs Data: Watching Shipments, Not Just Monthly Totals

markDefs.definition: India's Directorate General of Commercial Intelligence and Statistics, the government body under the Ministry of Commerce and Industry that compiles and publishes India's official foreign trade statistics.

children.text: India's official export and import totals, compiled by

, give you the country-level picture but with real reporting lag and no company-level detail. A separate layer of private vendors, in the same spirit as global providers like Panjiva and ImportGenius, aggregate customs bills of lading into shipment-level records, letting you see which specific companies are shipping what, to whom, and how volumes are trending well before any of it shows up in a quarterly filing.

body.caption: Aggregate trade data and shipment-level customs data trade breadth for granularity

cells: Breadth
Covers all of India's trade, by product category and partner country
Covers only the shipments the vendor has captured, which can miss smaller exporters
Directness
Tells you the national trend, not any specific company's trend
Tells you a specific company's shipment activity directly, if it appears in the data
Cost
Free, published by the government
Priced as a commercial product, reflecting the processing work to structure raw customs records

children.text: Job Postings and Hiring Velocity: The IT Services Read

Hiring velocity matters most where headcount growth is directly tied to revenue growth, which describes India's IT services sector almost perfectly: companies like TCS, Infosys, and Wipro scale revenue largely by adding billable employees, so a slowdown in hiring intent is one of the earliest visible signs of a demand slowdown, often well before it shows up in reported revenue growth. Naukri's JobSpeak Index, published by Info Edge, is a real, widely cited Indian hiring activity index that analysts already watch for exactly this reason.

body.title: A Hiring Signal That Contradicts the Earnings Call
body.scenario: On its latest earnings call, a large IT services company's leadership expresses confidence about a strong pipeline for the coming year, with only routine, well supported answers to analyst questions on demand, similar in tone to Company A's specific, well grounded response from the previous lesson's exercise. At the same time, hiring activity trackers for the IT sector, including fresher and lateral job postings, show a marked slowdown building over the prior two quarters.
body.prompt: How should a researcher weigh the confident, well grounded management commentary against the hiring slowdown, and what would you check next before drawing a conclusion?
body.modelAnswer: The two signals are not necessarily contradictory, and the right move is not to simply pick one over the other. Confident, specific management commentary reduces the concern that comes from evasive hedging language, but it does not fully explain away a broad-based hiring slowdown, since companies sometimes hold a cautiously optimistic public tone even as internal capacity planning quietly turns more conservative. Before drawing a conclusion, check whether the hiring slowdown is company-specific or sector-wide, whether it concerns fresher hiring alone (often tied to expected future growth) or also lateral hiring (often tied to current project ramp-ups), and whether utilization rates and bench commentary elsewhere in the transcript are consistent with strong near-term demand. A sector-wide slowdown concentrated in lateral hiring, alongside otherwise confident commentary, is worth treating as an early caution flag rather than dismissing outright just because the call itself sounded reassuring.

children.text: MCA21: Reading the Corporate Registry for Group and Private Company Activity

markDefs.definition: India's Ministry of Corporate Affairs portal for company filings, including incorporations, director appointments and resignations, and charges (security interests) created or satisfied against a company's assets.

children.text: covers every registered company in India, listed or not, which makes it uniquely useful for watching a promoter's private group entities, the ones that never file exchange announcements but that Chapter 1's governance discussion showed can still leak cash out of a listed company. A fresh charge creation against a private group company's assets, a new subsidiary incorporated shortly before an unrelated announcement, or a wave of director resignations across group entities are all visible here, often well before any of it surfaces in the listed company's own related party transaction note.

body.title: Why MCA21 is harder to work with than it sounds

children.text: Unlike a clean API, MCA21 filings are often searched and retrieved company by company, and details within a filing, such as the specific terms of a charge, may require opening individual documents rather than reading a structured field. Building a systematic MCA21 monitoring pipeline across an entire promoter group's private entities is realistic, but it is a genuine data engineering project, not a quick script, which is exactly the kind of build-vs-buy trade-off covered later in Chapter 3.

body.title: A Quick MCA21 Check on a Promoter Group
steps: List the promoter group's known private entities from the listed company's related party transaction note and shareholding pattern
Search each private entity on MCA21 for recent charge creation or satisfaction filings
Note any new incorporations by the same promoters or directors in the last one to two years
Check for overlapping directorships between the listed company and its private group entities
Cross-reference any new charges or loans against the amounts disclosed in the listed company's related party transaction note
Flag any mismatch between what MCA21 shows and what has been disclosed to shareholders for closer review

body.text: This whole category rewards patience over cleverness. E-way bills, customs records, job postings, and MCA21 filings are not exciting to read, which is exactly why they are underused, and exactly why they still carry a genuine informational edge.

Companies and vendor categories named in this lesson illustrate concepts only and are not recommendations to trade any security or endorsements of any specific vendor. Always verify current thresholds, procedures, and terms of use directly with the relevant government portal or data provider before building a pipeline on top of it.
